name: JEDI axion search
full_name: Jülich Electric Dipole moment Investigations — axion search
summary: JEDI uses polarized deuteron beams for an axion dark-matter proof of principle, as a dedicated dark-matter analysis of an electric-dipole-moment research facility.
detection_principle: Scanning beam momentum changes the spin-precession frequency; resonance with an axion field accumulates polarization perpendicular to the ring plane.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2022 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: First Search for Axion-Like Particles in a Storage Ring Using a Polarized Deuteron Beam

collaboration.name: JEDI axion search Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No ALP resonance was observed; upper limits were set on the deuteron's oscillating electric dipole moment and axion coupling.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
